evidence:
Pairwise review of all 53 criteria (gates are 0-weight prerequisites and excluded from double-credit concerns). Strengths: many explicit ownership boundaries prevent duplication: hro_arrive_bottom (functional judge.toml:65) 'Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move'; hro_pol_live_thread (polish judge.toml:32) 'This row owns the draft and focus; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional'; hro_thread_earlier (paging/count) vs hro_pol_earlier_place (scroll anchor) are disjoint; hro_candidate_no_staff (candidate writes) vs hro_candidate_private (candidate reads) vs hro_observer_readonly vs hro_anonymous split by actor; undo rows split by condition (restores/conflict/once/full). No pair demands incompatible products: hro_move_one_stage skip refusal vs hro_mgr_late_stages Interview->Offer->Hired->back, hro_reject_hired vs hro_mgr_late_stages, hro_add_candidate bottom-of-Applied vs hro_undo_restores original-place are each consistent with hireops_rules.md:47-65,94-100. Visual likert rows overlap conceptually but visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row'.

DEFECT (subsumption + contradictory judge instruction): hro_candidate_linked (functional judge.toml:393-399, weight 0.5, 'the card added with Tomas's account email becomes Tomas's application and conversation when he signs in') is strictly subsumed by hro_msg_exchange (judge.toml:294-300, weight 1.5, 'Rafael's message reaches Tomas's independent context'), because protocol T (functional/prompt.md:39) runs the exchange only on 'Tomas's new J2 conversation' created by that linking (fallback J3 is also a linked card). hro_unread_counts (judge.toml:330-336, 2.0: 'On Tomas's new J2 conversation, after Tomas's two messages') and hro_seen (judge.toml:348-354, 1.5: 'after Tomas opens it') and hro_candidate_view's wording-follows-stage leg (judge.toml:375-381, 1.5; protocol K prompt.md:43 moves 'Tomas's J2 card') also require the same linking as setup. Every app that passes hro_msg_exchange passes hro_candidate_linked; a single linking defect is graded in up to five rows (0.5+1.5+2+1.5+1.5 = 7.0 of 58.5 functional weight, ~12% of functional, ~7% of total reward). Meanwhile functional/prompt.md:23 says 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' and prompt.md:13 says re-setup 'on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature', which is impossible here (any Tomas conversation on a new job needs linking) and the seeded Data Analyst conversation is only named as an exclusion (prompt.md:39 'not his Data Analyst one'), so the judge has two incompatible instructions: fail the dependent rows on the observed linking defect, or refrain from double deduction and leave them unobserved/passed. Scoring of the same app can therefore differ by up to 7 weight points depending on which instruction the judge follows. This is the 'subsume each other' case in the workbook wording, not the permitted 'one criterion covering a whole flow' bundle (SKILL.md known false positives), and REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping ... Preserve valid observations' requires distinct promises (live message delivery, per-person unread, seen marks) to be observable independently of the linking promise.

Same pattern, lower confidence (Notes inside this Fail): (a) Interview capacity: an app with no capacity check fails hro_interview_full (1.5), hro_refused_put_back (2.0; pinned to 'the page that tried the full-Interview move', judge.toml:137, although any refused move e.g. the skip in M would show put-back per rules:82-85), hro_bulk_places (1.5) and hro_undo_full (0.5) = 5.5 weight for one defect; additionally hro_interview_full's 'that card stays where it was' and hro_refused_put_back's 'Fails if the card stays in the wrong stage' can both be read as the UI revert, double-deducting a client-only revert bug. (b) Skip enforcement: hro_move_one_stage (1.5) and hro_bulk_all_or_none (2.0) both fail when the server never refuses a skip, because the all-or-none probe uses a skip (prompt.md:35 step 5) plus capacity (step 7). (c) hro_undo_once leg 2 (judge.toml:254) is replayed at B step 11 after the V-and-X move is already blocked by Mei's conflicting move (step 9-10), so it re-observes hro_undo_conflict's refusal and cannot independently show 'later move supersedes'. (d) Live-update preconditions: hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread score 0 when no update arrives (polish judge.toml:23,32), so a no-polling app loses both functional liveness rows and polish preservation rows; this is justified (preservation is unobservable without arrival; REVIEW_POLICY dead feature must not earn credit) and acceptable. (e) Prompt-vs-criterion contradiction: functional/prompt.md:19 'A refused action may add a generic log line' vs hro_activity_refusals (judge.toml:271) 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line' and hireops_rules.md:113 'A refused action adds no entry' (row 33 owner should also see this).

No runtime evidence applies: raw-evidence-index.json scope states full configured grading is absent; this verdict is a static rubric-structure finding and is NOT EXERCISED by any judge run.
counterexample: An otherwise complete app whose add-candidate endpoint stores the email but never links the new card to an existing candidate account (Tomas only sees his seeded Data Analyst application). Protocol T's 'Tomas's new J2 conversation' never appears for Tomas: hro_candidate_linked=0 (correct), and hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_seen and the wording-change leg of hro_candidate_view cannot be observed and are scored 0 (or, if the judge obeys prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row', some of them are passed/unscored), even though live delivery, per-person unread counts and seen marks all work correctly on Tomas's seeded conversation. One defect costs up to 7.0/58.5 functional weight, and the outcome depends on which conflicting instruction the judge follows. Conversely a correct app always earns hro_candidate_linked whenever it earns hro_msg_exchange, so the 0.5 row adds no independent signal there.
suggested_fix: Decouple setup from the linking promise: run hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts and hro_seen on Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation (state-relative counts) or explicitly instruct the judge to fall back to it when the new J2 card does not reach Tomas, keep hro_candidate_linked as the sole owner of linking, and likewise let hro_refused_put_back use any observed refused move and state which row owns a server-capacity versus UI-revert defect; reconcile prompt.md:19 with hro_activity_refusals.
